paper_title: DraftAttention: Fast Video Diffusion via Low-Resolution Attention Guidance
original_abstract: Diffusion transformer-based video generation models (DiTs) have recently attracted widespread attention for their excellent generation quality. However, their computational cost remains a major bottleneck—attention alone accounts for over 80% of total latency, and generating just 8 seconds of 720p video takes tens of minutes—posing serious challenges to practical application and scalability. To address this, we propose the DraftAttention, a training-free framework for the acceleration of video diffusion transformers with dynamic sparse attention on GPUs. We apply down-sampling to each feature map across frames in the compressed latent space, enabling a higher-level receptive field over the latent composed of hundreds of thousands of tokens. The low-resolution draft attention map, derived from draft query and key, exposes redundancy both spatially within each feature map and temporally across frames. We reorder the query, key, and value based on the draft attention map to guide the sparse attention computation in full resolution, and subsequently restore their original order after the attention computation. This reordering enables structured sparsity that aligns with hardware-optimized execution. Our theoretical analysis demonstrates that the low-resolution draft attention closely approximates the full attention, providing reliable guidance for constructing accurate sparse attention. Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing sparse attention approaches in video generation quality and achieves up to 1.75× end-to-end speedup on GPUs.

proposed_runtime.sparse_attention: [n, n·r, d] where r is sparsity ratio

innovative_points.name: Low-Resolution Draft Attention
innovative_points.description: Uses aggressive 8×16 average pooling to create lightweight draft attention maps that guide sparse computation
innovative_points.novelty: First to apply extreme downsampling (128× token reduction) for attention guidance in video diffusion

runtime_change.after: [g, g, d] → O(g²d) where g = n/128

innovative_points.name: Hardware-Friendly Reordering
innovative_points.description: Deterministic token reordering to align sparse patterns with contiguous memory blocks
innovative_points.novelty: First to address memory alignment for video diffusion sparse attention

innovative_points.name: Training-Free Dynamic Sparsity
innovative_points.description: Generates sparse patterns on-the-fly without additional training or warm-up
innovative_points.novelty: First truly dynamic sparse attention for video diffusion (vs static SVG, warm-up AdaSpa)

runtime_change.after: Dynamic r% sparsity per attention module
runtime_change.flexibility: Sparsity adapts per module, per timestep

innovative_points.name: Vision-Centric Redundancy Analysis
innovative_points.description: Identifies spatial and temporal redundancy specifically for video generation
innovative_points.novelty: First systematic analysis of attention redundancy in video diffusion transformers
innovative_points.practical_insight: 80% attention computation is redundant in video generation

improvements.name: Adaptive Multi-Scale Draft Attention (AMDA)
improvements.description: Use multiple pooling kernels (4×4, 8×8, 16×16) with learned importance weights
improvements.implementation: Lightweight MLP to predict scale importance

improvements.name: Motion-Aware Temporal Pooling (MATP)
improvements.description: Use optical flow to guide temporal pooling, preserving motion boundaries

runtime_analysis.guided_pooling: [g_t, g_t, d] with motion weights → O(g_t²d)

improvements.practical_impact: Better motion preservation in generated videos

improvements.name: Hybrid Sparse-Quantized Attention (HSQA)
improvements.description: Combine sparsity with INT4 quantization for query/key projections
improvements.implementation: INT4 for Q/K, FP16 for V to maintain precision

improvements.name: In-Place Reordering with Shared Memory
improvements.description: Use GPU shared memory for in-place reordering to eliminate memory copy

improvements.name: Dynamic Layer-wise Sparsity (DLS)
improvements.description: Predict optimal sparsity ratio per layer using lightweight MLP on layer statistics

runtime_analysis.sparsity_prediction: [l, h, 1] → O(lh) where l=layers, h=hidden stats
runtime_analysis.adaptation: Sparsity changes per layer and timestep

architecture.quantization: INT4 Q/K, FP16 V hybrid approach

runtime_analysis.scalability: 2× longer sequences within same memory budget
